feedback.description: AC mechanism literalism / spec-contract mismatch on the synthetic-handle prefix. The authored AC-13 acceptance test data-guardrails.test.ts:32 asserts `expect(p.handle).toMatch(/^synthetic-handle-/)`, and setup/test-helpers.ts (lines 63, 90, 118-121) keys every synthetic profile and SEEDED_IDENTITY_MAP by the literal prefix `synthetic-handle-NNN`. The plan and SUB-TASK-1 instead specify the handle as `handle-<n>` (SUB-TASK-1 line 16: 'one IdentityMapping per employee keyed by a synthetic handle (`handle-<n>`...)') and describe it only as generic 'handle-prefixed' (implementation-plan.md:122, :138, :166 TS-P1-04; test-scenarios.json TS-P1-04 line 80, TS-P3-02 line 235). A seed that emits `handle-7` does NOT match `/^synthetic-handle-/`, so the AC-13 guardrail test the plan explicitly claims to make resolve/GREEN via `lib/dev/guardrails.ts:loadSeedProfiles` fails RED. SKILL-1's own loosely-worded scenarios ('handle-prefixed') would still pass against the wrong prefix, masking the defect. This is a genuinely new gap, not raised in iterations 1/2 (F-01 tsx, F-02 DB mechanism, F-03/R2-01 count, R2-02 datasourceUrl, R2-03 no-name projection). All other review categories pass this clean-slate review: counts reconcile (20 scenarios / 44 files [38 create / 6 modify] / 3 ADRs across plan, test-scenarios.json header counts field AND enumerated ids, output JSON, STORY.md, metadata; historical iter-1/2 event counts correctly preserved as audit trail). The 3 tactical ADRs are correctly-scoped, justified deviations. F-01 seed wiring (tsx devDependency + prisma.config.ts migrations.seed='tsx prisma/seed.ts' + `prisma db push && prisma db seed`) and the F-02 runtime test-DB mechanism (`new PrismaClient({ datasourceUrl: process.env.DATABASE_URL })` + Vitest globalSetup DATABASE_URL override + dev.db guard) are internally consistent and verified against the actual repo: schema datasource block (prisma/schema.prisma:9-11) is `provider="sqlite"` with no url/env(); prisma.config.ts is CLI-scope only; starter @@unique keys (EmployeeSkill, Enrollment, Skill.name) and the leadId self-relation are preserved; the `tags`->`tagsJson` rename is safe (single producer/consumer). loadSeedProfiles() correctly projects away the `name` column (R2-03 resolved). The UPPER<->hyphen value-map bridge (TACTICAL-ADR-01) matches test-helpers.ts:42-58. The injectable Claude client shape `{ createMessage(args) -> { content:[{type:'text',text}] } }` matches test-helpers. Phase ordering (P1 schema -> P2 repo/wrapper -> P1 seed -> P3 tests), diff budget (~700-900 LOC within L), and reuse-vs-build decisions are defensible.
feedback.suggestion: Pin the synthetic handle to the literal prefix `synthetic-handle-` everywhere it is specified so the seed and loadSeedProfiles() projection satisfy the authored AC-13 assertion `/^synthetic-handle-/`. Concretely: (1) Update SUB-TASK-1 pseudocode and implementation-plan.md (Wiring Trace line 122 and AC/BR Mechanism Map line 138) to specify handles as `synthetic-handle-<n>` (e.g. `synthetic-handle-001`), not `handle-<n>`. (2) Tighten TS-P1-04 (test-scenarios.json line 80) and TS-P3-02 (line 235) THEN clauses to assert the EXACT prefix `synthetic-handle-` (match `/^synthetic-handle-/`) rather than generic 'handle-prefixed', so SKILL-1's own foundation no-PII test cannot false-green against a wrong prefix. (3) Ensure prisma/seed.ts writes IdentityMapping.syntheticHandle values with that exact prefix and that the seeded handles align with the deterministic SEEDED_IDENTITY_MAP keys the ported acceptance tests expect.
